thread.title: This Cornell University student finds cheap flights online for people — for free

author: Maria LaMagna
title: This Cornell University student finds cheap flights online for people — for free
text:
“I will find you cheap flights (again) for free. All I ask is that you think about doing something nice for someone else :)” That was the message a Reddit poster named “delta777er” posted this month, to a subreddit dedicated to being frugal.
Requests poured in, asking for help finding flights from Seattle to Alaska, from Melbourne, Australia to Salt Lake City, Utah, from Cairo to London. “Hey man I think it is great that you are doing this for the people who are having a hard time doing it for themselves,” one commenter said, who got help flying from New York to Dublin. “Thank you so much for posting this!” another said, flying from Minneapolis to St. Louis.
It turns out, delta777er is Nick Doyle, a 21-year-old junior at Cornell University, studying computer science. He was able to answer about 30 inquiries.
Courtesy of Nick Doyle Nick Doyle has interned for Southwest Airlines in software development. MarketWatch asked him a few questions:
MarketWatch: How did you become interested in finding flights online?
Doyle: Since I was about five years old, I’ve loved aviation and traveling, and it’s always been a hobby of mine.
I was always doing it for myself, finding random cities and seeing what kind of flights are available ...like putting a point on a map and trying to find a way to a far-off place. I thought, instead of doing random cities for myself, it would be equally interesting to find it for other people.
MarketWatch: How did you decide to use Reddit, with your instruction to pay it forward?
Doyle: I did this a couple of other times, but didn’t get the same number of responses.
It was actually kind of fun seeing this post reach a lot of people. Most of the time it’s a very confusing process if you’re not heavily into aviation to find the best airlines to fly on. Some people in the comments said what they were planning to go on the trip for their honeymoons or to visit family members they haven’t seen in a long time. I thought that was really fun, and it’s cool how aviation connects everyone.
MarketWatch: What are your best tips for finding cheap flights?
Doyle: The number one rule is to be flexible.
A big thing about airlines is that they differentiate between business travelers and leisure travelers. They try to charge business travelers more, who travel closer to the deadline and are less flexible. You want to be as flexible as you can, so you don’t get shoved in with ‘business traveler’ kind of places. 
So that’s why you want to book early and be flexible with your hours. Also, flying to an airport that might not be the closest to your destination. 
[Editor’s note: Flying John F. Kennedy Airport in New York to Heathrow in London is one such example, Doyle said. But even more than routes, booking early is key to avoiding higher fares, he said. And flying on mid-weekdays can be less expensive than a Friday or Monday flight, when business travelers are more likely to be flying. San Jose and Oakland airports can also have cheaper fares than San Francisco International Airport, he said.] 
MarketWatch: What sites do you like to use to find cheap flights?
Doyle: I use Kayak BKNG, +0.86% and Momondo, a Danish site. Those are good if you have a specific route you want to take. Google Flights, or the lesser-known Google site GOOG, +0.10% ITA Matrix. But for some people who don’t have a particular trip in mind, it’s good to use Kiwi. That’s great for more of backpack travel … it might not give you the most direct way.
MarketWatch: Are there any other blogs or resources you like to look at?
Doyle: TheFlightDeal.com , they just post daily deals.I also read Skift, for articles about aviation.
MarketWatch: Is there a certain day of the week you think is best for booking flights?
Doyle: Wednesday is the best. But it’s not that it lowers the price that much. Booking early is a lot better than just booking on a Wednesday.
MarketWatch: What are the best trips you’ve booked for yourself?
Doyle: Sophomore year, I found flights to Japan for $400, round trip from New York. I went with four other college friends, but I was the one who did the flights. It was during our six-week winter break, right after New Year’s. We flew Air China through Beijing. We were just really lucky. We booked it seven months early.
We were originally thinking about Cancun, but then we saw the deal in July, and it was about the same price. We thought you can’t pass that up.
MarketWatch: Do you have any favorite airlines?
Doyle: In terms of international, Norwegian NWARF, +6.56% is probably the best for transatlantic. I went this winter break to Ireland for $250. I was thinking it would be a lot worse. [Editor’s note: The airline doesn’t provide free food or beverages onboard. It also flies from Stewart International Airport, about 65 miles north of New York City, to Dublin.]
MarketWatch: What are your plans for the future?
Doyle: This summer I’m going out to San Francisco for my internship. I’ll be interning at Apple. AAPL, +0.20% Then in the fall, I’m going back to Southwest Airlines LUV, +3.30% for my fall internship. Right now I’m taking it week by week, but I’d love to work for a tech company or an aviation company. It’s cool to see how fast technology is growing in the aviation industry.
